title: GEOS Aerosols (2025)
description: Aerosols modeled by NASA's Goddard Earth Observing System (GEOS) on 19 August 2025, 20:00 UTC. NASA colours four types: sea salt (blue), dust (pink/magenta), smoke from fires (orange/red; 'Black Carbon' on the colour bar) and sulfates from pollution and volcanoes (green).

files.role: analysed: every sound is computed from these pixels
files.note: 8-bit RGB PNG with no colour profile or gamma chunk, so browsers decode exactly these bytes.

files.role: analysed: the four aerosol colours are read from this colour bar
display only: texture for the spinning 3D globe
files.method: macOS sips: resampled to 2048 × 1024 (2:1 for a sphere), JPEG quality 85

files.role: display only: record sleeve on the shelf and the 3D jukebox
files.method: macOS sips: resampled to 640 × 360, JPEG quality 82

retrievalNote: svs.gsfc.nasa.gov timed out from this network on 14 Nov 2026, so the files were retrieved from the Internet Archive's captures of NASA's original URLs (raw 'id_' responses). Re-verify the hashes against NASA's live files when reachable.

credits.producer: NASA's Global Modeling and Assimilation Office (GMAO) and NASA's Scientific Visualization Studio (SVS)
credits.dataset: GEOS-FP 2Km Replay (GEOS Forward Processing 2Km Replay), model

limits: GEOS is a model analysis that assimilates satellite observations, in situ measurements and about one million weather observations per hour; it is not a direct measurement. The colour bar has no numeric scale, so TerraJuke reports rendered colour strength, never aerosol optical depth or concentration.
